chunks: He asked: 'What was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph?' They said: 'God preserve us; we knew no evil in him.' The wife of the minister said: 'Now the truth has become clear; I sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful.'
ai.seo_question: What did the wife of the Aziz say about Joseph's character when the truth was revealed?
ai.summary: In this pivotal moment from Surah Yusuf, the King (Al-Malik) questions the women who accompanied the wife of the Aziz, leading to their testimony of Joseph's innocence. The wife of the Aziz then confesses, stating 'Now the truth has become evident' (ḥaṣḥaṣa al-ḥaqq), acknowledging Joseph's truthfulness and virtue, which serves as the turning point for his eventual release from prison. Shia scholars often highlight this confession as a divine vindication of the Prophets' chastity and a demonstration of how truth emerges even from the mouths of the accusers.
